post.caption: Linnaeus once farmed pearls in mussels. Swedish naturalist Carl Linnaeus grew freshwater pearls in river mussels by slipping a tiny limestone pellet through the shell. In 1761, he offered the method to the Swedish state, and a state committee approved it. In 1762, he sold the secret to the Gothenburg merchant Peter Bagge, and the king's decree gave Bagge the right to use it. Bagge could not make it pay, and the instructions were lost. The Linnean Society in London keeps Linnaeus's pearls.
